design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 44 participants were randomly allocated to probiotic soy milk or conventional soy milk, so it is a randomized parallel-group trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation was explicitly described as random and baseline biochemical measures were similar, the sequence-generation method and allocation-concealment procedure were not reported; one dietary baseline imbalance was observed and adjusted for.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 44 participants were randomly allocated to the soy milk group (control) or probiotic soy milk group

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was described as double-blinded, intervention adherence was monitored and generally good, and co-interventions were standardized, but the identities of all blinded parties, blinding success, and use of intention-to-treat analysis were not reported; analyses appear restricted to completers.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Adherence was good in 90% of of the participants who used at least 50 bottles out of 56 bottles of their probiotic or conventional soy milk.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 40 of 44 randomized participants (90.9%), with balanced attrition across groups, but reasons included loss to follow-up and poor adherence and no sensitivity analysis established that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Forty-four patients participated, and 40 completed the study (20 patients in each group; Figure).

domain_judgments.rationale: Kidney-related outcomes were measured using objective biochemical assays applied consistently across groups, and laboratory testing was performed blinded, paired, in the same run, and in random order.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All the tests were performed in a blinded fashion, in pairs (before and after the intervention) at the same time, in the same analytic run, and in random order to reduce systematic error and interassay variability.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and primary endpoints were identified, but the text does not establish that registration occurred prospectively or provide enough protocol detail to exclude selective choice among change-score, post-intervention, paired, unadjusted, and adjusted analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study protocol was registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (Register code: IRCT201601027479N2 available at: http://www.irct.ir).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Objective blinded outcome measurement supports low risk in that domain, but random-sequence generation and allocation concealment were insufficiently described, the analysis appears limited to completers, and selective analysis/reporting cannot be excluded despite trial registration.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports computer-generated random allocation, with stratification by age, BMI, sex, and medication, to probiotic or placebo groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated, stratified random sequence was used, but the report does not describe allocation concealment before assignment, and some baseline metabolic values show potentially meaningful numerical imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was carried out using computer-generated random numbers by a trained staff member at the internal clinic.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants received matching placebo capsules under double-blinding, adherence was monitored, co-intervention indicators such as diet were similar, and all randomized participants were analyzed according to intention to treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The placebo group received capsules in similar shape and packaging as the probiotic... The analyses were done based on the intention-to-treat approach (ITT).

domain_judgments.rationale: Six of 60 participants (10%), equally distributed between groups, withdrew for personal reasons, and the investigators used last observation carried forward, an assumption-sensitive method that does not establish that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the patients in the probiotic group, 3 patients [withdrawn due to personal reasons (n = 3)], and in the placebo group, 3 persons [withdrawn due to personal reasons (n = 3)] were excluded... The missing values were treated based on the Last-Observation-Carried-Forward (LOCF) method.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome HOMA-IR was derived from fasting glucose and insulin measured using objective, standardized laboratory procedures applied equally to both groups, and double-blinding reduced the likelihood that knowledge of assignment influenced measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the baseline and end-of-treatment, 15 mL blood samples were obtained from each patient at the Kashan reference laboratory in the early morning after an overnight fast... Serum insulin values were quantified by the use of an available ELISA kit.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and identifies HOMA-IR as primary, but the paper reports many metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative-stress, renal, and gene-expression outcomes without enough protocol or analysis-plan detail to rule out selective choice among eligible analyses or measurements.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This clinical trial was registered by the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (http://www.irct.ir: # IRCT2017061134458N1)... The primary outcome variable was HOMA-IR.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, 10% missing data handled with LOCF, and insufficient information to exclude selective reporting across numerous outcomes and analyses; objective blinded outcome measurement and ITT analysis otherwise reduce risk.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly allocated 1:1 to probiotic or placebo, with a manually generated simple randomization sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation concealment and baseline comparability were adequate, but the report only says the sequence was manually generated and does not explain the random mechanism sufficiently to verify sequence generation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The random sequence of treatment (probiotic and placebo) was manually generated for a simple randomization. None of the subjects involved in the study had access to the allocation sequence until the end of the statistical analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and relevant researchers were blinded and adherence was monitored, but adherence was imperfect and analyses appear restricted to completers rather than intention-to-treat, with 13 of 46 randomized participants excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Adherence was high with 82% of patients (placebo and probiotics) consuming more than 80% of the capsules.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for 13 of 46 randomized participants (28.3%), and no reasons by group or analyses demonstrating that missingness could not bias the results were reported; microbiota outcomes were available for only 20 participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Seven patients in the probiotic group and 6 in the placebo group left the study (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured with objective laboratory methods applied consistently across groups, and laboratory personnel were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All laboratory measurements were centralized and performed in a blinded manner.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while numerous outcomes and both within-group and between-group analyses created scope for selective reporting or emphasis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The differences of the variable were analyzed using nonparametric tests (paired tests, Wilcoxon) or parametric tests (Independent Samples t-test or Paired Samples t-test). The percentage delta (D) was also used to check the differences in the variables before and after supplementation.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial missing outcome data and complete-case analysis after 13 of 46 randomized participants withdrew, without evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcomes. Additional concerns arise from incompletely described sequence generation, lack of intention-to-treat analysis, and no reported preregistration or analysis plan.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized parallel trial: allocation used computer-generated random numbers after matching, with probiotic and placebo groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence and stated concealment support random allocation, but one nutritionist generated/implemented allocation and several biochemical outcomes differed at baseline, leaving some concern about concealment and chance imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization assignment was conducted using computer-generated random numbers. Randomization and allocation were hidden from the researchers and patients until the final analyses were completed.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with placebo control, adherence exceeded 90% in both groups, and all randomized participants were included under an intention-to-treat analysis, with no important intervention-related deviations reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: On average, the rate of compliance in our study was high, such that >90% of probiotic and placebo capsules were consumed throughout the study in both groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Five of 60 participants withdrew and were nevertheless included in an intention-to-treat analysis, but the method used to impute or otherwise handle their missing 12-week outcomes is not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two participants in the probiotic group and 3 participants in the placebo group withdrew due to personal reasons, and were excluded from the study... However, because the analysis was done based on the intention-to-treat principle, all 60 participants (30 in each group) were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Most outcomes were objective laboratory measures assessed consistently, but assessor blinding is not clearly described and SGA was a subjective outcome administered by the main investigator, so knowledge of allocation could have influenced that measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The SGA questionnaire was also used by the same investigator after the 12-week intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered, the report evaluates many outcomes and presents both unadjusted and post hoc adjusted analyses, with some initially significant findings becoming nonsignificant, while no prespecified analysis plan is provided to establish that the reported results were selected independently of the data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: When we adjusted the analyses for baseline values of biochemical variables, the changes in HOMA-B (P = 0.06) and TAC levels (P = 0.24) were not significantly different between the groups (data not shown).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by high risk of selective reporting across numerous outcomes and alternative adjusted/unadjusted analyses without an available prespecified analysis plan. Additional concerns arise from baseline imbalances, unclear handling of missing outcomes despite claimed intention-to-treat analysis, and subjective SGA assessment.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 60 patients were randomly allocated using a random number table to probiotic or control honey.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random number table generated the allocation sequence and baseline demographic measures were similar, but allocation concealment until assignment was not described and baseline balance was incompletely assessed across prognostic factors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was done using a random number table by one of the investigators who had no clinical involvement in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial is described as double-blind, used control honey, and reports an intention-to-treat analysis, but it does not explain who was blinded, whether the products were indistinguishable, or how missing outcomes were handled in the ITT analysis; adherence was also monitored only through text messages.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The analyses were carried out based on intention-to-treat (ITT) principle.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only three of 60 randomized participants withdrew (5%), with similarly low attrition in both groups, so outcome data were available for nearly all participants and substantial bias from missingness is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, 57 participants [probiotic honey (n = 28) and control honey (n = 29)] completed the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes were objective laboratory biomarkers measured at the same time points in both groups using specified commercial or standardized assays with low assay variation, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Before the onset and after the end of the intervention, 10-mL fasting blood samples were obtained from each patient at Kashan reference laboratory.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration is cited and primary versus secondary outcomes are identified, but the text does not establish that a prespecified analysis plan was finalized before unblinded data were available, while numerous biomarkers and derived indices permit selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcomes were parameters of insulin metabolism in the current study. Secondary outcome variables were fasting plasma glucose (FPG), lipid profiles, biomarkers of inflammation, and oxidative stress, serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) concentrations.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by absent reporting of allocation concealment and incomplete details about blinding, adherence, ITT implementation, and prespecification of analyses. Attrition was low and laboratory outcome measurement was objective and consistent.
